statement: On a die, opposite faces add up to 7. Lily sees the top (1), the front (2) and the right face. Her three hidden faces add up to 14. What is on the right face?

choices.misconception: I found the hidden face that makes 14 with the 6 and the 5, which is 3, but that is the face opposite the right face, not the right face itself.
I thought the right face is opposite the front, so I gave $7 - 2 = 5$, but two opposite faces can never be seen at the same time.
I thought the right face is opposite the top, so I gave $7 - 1 = 6$, but two opposite faces can never be seen at the same time.
I worked out that the three faces Lily sees add up to $21 - 14 = 7$ and gave that total, forgetting to take away the 1 and the 2.

hints: Which faces are hidden, and which seen face is each one opposite?
Each hidden face is opposite one of the faces Lily sees, and every pair of opposite faces makes 7. You can use all six faces together, or find the hidden faces one at a time.
All six faces add up to $3 \times 7 = 21$, so the three faces Lily sees add up to $21 - 14 = 7$. The top and the front make $1 + 2 = 3$, so the right face shows $7 - 3 = 4$.

solutions.reliable: The hidden faces are the bottom, the back and the left. The bottom is opposite the 1, so it shows 6. The back is opposite the 2, so it shows 5. The three hidden faces add up to 14, so the left face shows $14 - 6 - 5 = 3$. The right face is opposite the left, so it shows $7 - 3 = 4$. Check: 4 is not opposite the 1 or the 2, so it can sit next to both of them. The transferable idea: every hidden face is the partner of a face you can see.
solutions.elegant: The three pairs of opposite faces make $3 \times 7 = 21$ in all. Take away the 14 that is hidden: the faces Lily sees make 7. So the right face is $7 - 1 - 2 = 4$.

whyOnTest: It checks using opposite faces making 7 both one pair at a time and as a total of 21, a favourite move in dice questions.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
